questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) The Central Processing Unit (CPU) of some computer systems contain single core processors while others contain multi-core processors.

(i) List the main components of a CPU. (3 marks)

(ii) With the aid of a diagram, explain briefly the machine cycle. (5 marks)

(iii) Explain why a multi-core processor computer will perform better than a single-core processor computer, with the same clock speed. (1 mark)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Main components of a CPU (3 marks, 1 each).** The **Arithmetic and Logic Unit (ALU)**, which does the calculations and the logical comparisons; the **Control Unit (CU)**, which fetches and decodes the instructions and coordinates the other parts; and the **registers** (small, very fast storage locations such as the program counter, the instruction register and the accumulator). (A cache memory is also accepted.)

**(ii) The machine cycle (5 marks).** The machine cycle (fetch-decode-execute cycle) is the sequence of steps that the CPU repeats for every instruction of a program stored in main memory.

![fig-1](gce-ol-computer-science-2024-p2-officiel-cameroun_exercice_4_fig_1.png)

1. **Fetch:** the address of the next instruction, held in the program counter (PC), is sent to main memory; the instruction is copied from memory into the instruction register (IR) and the PC is increased to point to the following instruction.
2. **Decode:** the control unit examines the instruction in the IR and works out the operation to perform (the opcode) and the data it needs (the operand).
3. **Execute:** the instruction is carried out, usually by the ALU (for example an addition), and the result is kept in a register or written back to memory.

The cycle then repeats with the next instruction until the program ends.

**(iii) Multi-core versus single-core (1 mark).** A multi-core processor has several cores, each able to run its own instructions at the same time (parallel processing), so with the same clock speed it completes more instructions, or more tasks, in the same time than a single core which handles them one after another.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(b) Newspaper layout editors use DTP software to design their newspapers.

(i) Give the full meaning of DTP. (1 mark)

(ii) Explain two advantages of DTP software over word processors in newspaper design. (4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) DTP (1 mark).** Desktop Publishing.

**(ii) Two advantages over a word processor (4 marks, 2 each).**

- **Precise page layout:** DTP software places text and pictures in frames that can be put anywhere on the page, in several columns, with text flowing from one frame to another and around pictures. A word processor treats the page mainly as a flow of text and cannot control the layout so exactly.
- **Professional output:** DTP software has better tools for graphics, fonts and colour, master pages and templates that keep every page consistent, and produces high-resolution, print-ready files for a printing press.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(c) What are the differences between the following?

(i) Compilers and Interpreters. (3 marks)

(ii) High Level Programming Language and Low Level Programming Language. (3 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Compiler and interpreter (3 marks).**

| Compiler | Interpreter |
|---|---|
| Translates the whole source program into machine code (object code) in one go before it runs. | Translates and executes the source program one statement at a time. |
| Produces an executable file that can be run again without the compiler. | Produces no executable file: the interpreter is needed every time the program runs. |
| Lists all the errors after the translation; the program runs faster. | Stops at the first error found, which makes debugging easier; the program runs more slowly. |

**(ii) High level and low level languages (3 marks).**

| High level language | Low level language |
|---|---|
| Close to human language (English-like), easy to read, write and debug (C, Pascal, Python). | Close to the machine's own instructions: machine code (binary) and assembly language. |
| Independent of the type of computer (portable); one statement gives several machine instructions. | Depends on the processor (not portable); one statement usually gives one machine instruction. |
| Needs a compiler or an interpreter to be translated. | Machine code needs no translation; assembly language needs an assembler. It runs faster and gives direct control of the hardware. |
